## The project type

```yaml
project:
  type: mcanouil
```

A pre-configured Quarto website: branded navbar, sidebar, footer, and favicon, with `mcanouil-html` as the default format.

## The formats

| Format | Output | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcanouil-html` | HTML | Professional or academic layouts. |
| `mcanouil-typst` | PDF, through Typst | Light and dark modes, and several document types: report, invoice, letter, CV. |
| `mcanouil-revealjs` | Slides | Light and dark modes, section outlines, and a closing slide. |

: The three format families. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[26,22,52]"}

Common options include `style`, choosing the layout, and `brand-mode`, choosing light or dark.

## What they share

- **Brand theming**, through `brand.yml`: colours, typography, and logos, consistent across all three.
- **Components**: value boxes, info panels, status badges, dividers, progress bars, card grids, and executive summaries.
- **Code windows**: window decoration on code blocks, in macOS, Windows, or plain style, with a filename and per-block overrides.
- **Grid background**: a subtle overlay, in HTML and RevealJS.
- **Special sections**: appendices and supplementary sections that relocate themselves and number separately, in Typst.
- **Accessibility**: PDF/UA-1 compliance, alt text, and WCAG AA contrast validation, in Typst.

## RevealJS options

Set under `extensions.mcanouil`, and enabled by the project type by default.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `section-outline` | `true` | Show a subsection outline on section slides. |
| `date-superscript` | `true` | Format ordinal dates as 1st, 2nd, 3rd. |
| `hide-title-slide-chrome` | `true` | Hide the menu, logo, and footer on the title slide. |
| `favicon-from-logo` | `true` | Generate a favicon from the slide logo. |
| `code-annotation-fragments` | `true` | Step through code annotations as fragments. |
| `debug-borders` | `false` | Draw borders on slide regions, for layout work. |

: RevealJS options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,12,58]"}

## Limitations

- The formats are opinionated by design: they are one person's brand rather than a neutral starting point.
- Typst-only features, the special sections and the accessibility checks among them, have no HTML equivalent.
